Mission Local’s November 29 data roundup highlighted four themes: turnout and registration, the Great Highway measure, campaign fundraising, and how redistricting shifted the electorates in Districts 5 and 7.

The story reported that about 412,000 people voted—38,000 fewer than in 2020, despite roughly the same number of registered voters. It also noted that Proposition H moved some races from odd to even years, when turnout is higher; that Proposition K passed 55–45 citywide despite opposition in districts near the Great Highway; and that fundraising did not guarantee a win for the measure. The roundup revisited how redistricting likely hurt Dean Preston and benefited Myrna Melgar.
